chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim quoted Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Abi Hamzah, on the authority of Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

He gathered all good into three traits: looking, being quiet, and talking. So every look in which there is no consideration is an oversight, and every silence in which there is no thought is heedlessness, and every speech in which there is no remembrance is vain talk. Blessed is he whose looking is a lesson, whose silence is thought, and whose speech is remembrance; who weeps for his sin, and saves people from his evil.

key_terms.اعْتِبَارٌ: Consideration or reflection; deriving a lesson from what is seen
key_terms.السُّكُوتُ: Silence or quietness; refraining from speech
key_terms.النَّظَرُ: Looking or sight; the act of observing with intent
key_terms.ذِكْرٌ: Remembrance; specifically of God, making speech meaningful
key_terms.عِبْرَةٌ: A lesson or moral example; the purpose of virtuous looking
key_terms.فِكْرَةٌ: Thought or contemplation; deep mental processing
key_terms.لَغْوٌ: Vain talk; speech devoid of meaning or divine remembrance

ai.seo_question: What are the three traits that contain all good according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* presents a triad of human faculties—sight, silence, and speech—rooted in the teachings of Imam Ali (AS) and transmitted through the chain of Abu Hamza al-Thumali to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It distinguishes between mere physical action and spiritual utility, defining true virtue as sight yielding lessons, silence fostering contemplation, and speech serving as divine remembrance. This framework emphasizes that moral integrity requires conscious intentionality in all sensory and communicative acts, ensuring one’s presence brings peace to others.
